newsitem.title: GERMANY: DMG initiates D.Telekom with overweight.
newsitem.headline: DMG initiates D.Telekom with overweight.

text.p: Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, the investment arm of Deutsche Bank AG, said on Friday it has initiated coverage of German telecommunications group Deutsche Telekom with a recommendation to overweight the stock.

DMG telecommunications analysts told Reuters in a telephone interview that the company stood by its earnings estimates for Deutsche Telekom, which predicted 35 percent compound growth in net earnings over the next five years.

"We are initiating coverage with an overweight recommendation, as you might expect," one DMG analyst said. "If they can deliver compound growth as predicted then there will surely be room for capital appreciation."
Another DMG analyst, explaining the evaluation, said: "By overweight, we mean that we believe it's going to outperform the DAX index."
Both analysts asked not to be identified.

Since its November 18 listing, Deutsche Telekom has underperformed the DAX index of 30 German blue chip stocks by 16 percent, closing floor trade down 53 pfennigs at 30.52 marks ($19.35) on Friday. The DAX was up 1.41 percent at 2,933.39 points.
But the fall in Telekom's share price from its initial trading price of 32.20 marks came as no surprise. The shares are still above the IPO price of 28.50 marks.
"It is fair to say that the offer price was at the high end of what was discussed ahead of the IPO. Frankly, I was surprised that it stayed as high as it did," one analyst said.
Another added: "We are very positive. Our story is exactly the same as it was at the time of the IPO."
-- William Boston, Bonn Newsroom, 49 228 26097150 ($ = 1.577 German Marks)
